citation: Durán et al. (2021), Revista Panamericana de Salud Pública
finding: 13 frameworks reported reliance: 12 national frameworks and one Caribbean shared system serving 15 countries.
comparison: Eight of the 12 positive national jurisdictions have directly extracted national authorisation wording in our 71-jurisdiction checkpoint; Costa Rica has narrower evidence, while Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay require further national-text recovery. Brazil’s later 2024 rule is a change over time, not a contradiction.
supporting_materials: Published law/year and framework tables preserved. Underlying source-document bundle available by request; not downloaded.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Colmagne Poulard et al. (2025), Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
finding: EMA reliance for initial applications met the study’s five-company reporting threshold in 26 countries. Its country table distinguishes practical reliance without a legal framework and a route reportedly not applied.
comparison: Tunisia and Morocco are evidence of reported practice without a legal framework; Turkey is a formal/practical-use discrepancy. These entries stay separate from national legal adoption dates.
supporting_materials: Original questionnaire DOCX and country-pathway XLSX downloaded; 70 unique countries matched, with duplicate Ghana/Rwanda route rows retained.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

scope: 21 responding African authorities out of 26 invited
finding: 20 of 21 authorities reported unilateral reliance. Among those answering the route question, 17 reported abridged, 14 verification and 10 recognition review; fewer reported legal frameworks supporting each route.
comparison: Supports separating actual use, route type and written authority. The participating-authority list includes Tanzania and Zanzibar, so 21 authorities cannot be treated as 21 distinct countries. The paper does not identify which single respondent lacked unilateral reliance.
supporting_materials: Public questionnaire PDF downloaded; tables preserved. No individual response dataset claimed.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

observation_period: Regulatory status through December 2025; collection completed February 2026
finding: Eight economies were included for new-drug reliance, six for new indications and seven for post-approval changes. Four of eight reported up to 30% additional submission workload; two reported meeting published new-drug timelines.
comparison: Seven of the eight new-drug economies have directly extracted national authorisation wording in our checkpoint; Indonesia has an official explanation. India’s limited provisions remain distinct from a general route. Public supporting responses permit country-specific checks of documentary and timing frictions.
supporting_materials: Country response PDF and March 2026 interim report downloaded. Supporting Vietnam link points to a finance circular; that link is flagged and is not used as pharmaceutical legal authority.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

finding: Maps regulatory agility, reliance, documentation and digital processes across economies.
comparison: Provides an earlier comparison point for the 2026 survey; emergency flexibilities, local trials and general authorisation reliance are coded separately.
supporting_materials: Public full text retrieved; public survey URL saved. That survey index returned a short/access response rather than a usable file.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Chong et al. (2022), Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
finding: Documents regulatory agility during the pandemic, including certificates, inspections and emergency reliance.
comparison: Its broad agility categories cannot establish a general new-drug authorisation route. The historical exclusions differ from later changes in the Philippines and Vietnam.
supporting_materials: Public full text and references retained; no separate response file recovered from this article.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Mangia et al. (2024), Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
scope: 48 authorities agreeing to a manufacturer pilot
finding: Describes an EMA-based pilot for a major manufacturing change to an already marketed monoclonal antibody. The planned global approval target was 6.5 months.
comparison: This is post-approval manufacturing work and a pilot target, not evidence that 48 countries have general new-drug recognition laws or achieved the target.
supporting_materials: Published country-requirement tables preserved. Retrieved supplementary archive contains figures only; article states no datasets generated/analysed.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Litsiou et al. (2026), Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
scope: 21 invited authorities; 13 confirmed participants; 19 tabled recipients
observation_period: Submissions by early October 2024; pilot endpoint May 2025 and later updates
finding: Reports shorter reviews relative to stated standard timelines for one oncology indication extension, with two countries pending in the published table.
comparison: Nineteen country rows are retained separately from law availability. Six recipients did not confirm pilot participation; Nigeria’s reported zero saving differs from the signed 3 minus 7 month gap. Abstract, completed-within-target and broader participant averages use different denominators and are not pooled.
supporting_materials: Published country timeline table preserved. No separate underlying dataset identified; supplementary archive contains figures only.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Dube-Mwedzi et al. (2025), Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice
observation_period: Applications received 2013–2018; registration follow-up to June 2022
finding: Reports 152 of 235 assessed products registered and a median seven months from joint recommendation to national registration, compared with a three-month target.
comparison: Shows why shared review recommendations and national authorisations need separate dates. Its table lists product-country counts, which must not be added as distinct products.
supporting_materials: Public supplemental DOCX downloaded; published country registration table preserved. Other underlying data described as available from the corresponding author; not requested.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Sithole et al. (2022), Frontiers in Medicine
scope: Industry applicants to the ZaZiBoNa process
finding: Applicants reported efficiencies and remaining barriers in the regional work-sharing process.
comparison: Used as operational experience, separate from national legal permission and comparative causal review-time estimates.
supporting_materials: Public supplemental questionnaire PDF downloaded. Raw response data available on request, not downloaded.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

scope: South African backlog sample and an African fee review
finding: Estimates US$277,413 in reviewer cost savings across 188 reliance applications; 25 of 33 industry respondents would consider higher fees when reliance works effectively.
comparison: A regulator-resource mechanism compatible with the legal-text analysis; estimated assessor savings do not measure medicine prices or patient welfare.
supporting_materials: Published cost and fee tables preserved. Supplementary archive contains figures only; underlying SAHPRA internal budget is not claimed downloaded.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

scope: Selected medicines/vaccines and high-burden sub-Saharan settings
finding: Describes a typical four-to-seven-year interval from first regulatory submission to final approval in the studied African destinations.
comparison: Combines several sequential stages; it is not a four-to-seven-year estimate of regulator processing time alone. Useful for the submission versus review decomposition.
supporting_materials: Public article/figures retained. Underlying third-party data subject to confidentiality agreements; private data not downloaded.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Ortiz-Prado et al. (2026), Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
finding: The abstract describes a structured legal/practice review covering product eligibility, reference authorities, assessment reports, sameness and local obligations.
comparison: Its abstract supports the same multidimensional approach, but country-specific results cannot be verified from the accessible abstract.
supporting_materials: Publisher abstract/reference page saved; full text is subscription-only and no public supporting file was found.
access: Public abstract/preview only; full text restricted
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text

citation: Perehudoff et al. (2021), The Lancet Regional Health – Europe
scope: 109 publications on EU influence in lower- and middle-income countries
finding: Distinguishes explicit agreements, reliance on EU rules or assessments, and softer channels such as funding and capacity building.
comparison: Gives a broader economic and institutional setting for our reference-authority network. These channels cannot all be coded as national drug-authorisation reliance.
supporting_materials: Two public supporting DOCX files downloaded, including search/protocol materials; original article tables preserved.

scope: Seven Latin American drug registers and EMA oncology approvals
finding: For 13 EMA-approved oncology drugs in the later cohort with no supporting trial or no trial assessed at low risk of bias, the seven national registers recorded approval of between eight and eleven drugs.
comparison: Provides a quality-of-evidence angle on international transmission of regulatory decisions. Approval overlap alone does not identify use of reliance; Brazil’s pre-2024 approvals are especially important for avoiding that inference.
supporting_materials: Public full text and original tables retrieved. Article states all relevant data are within the manuscript; supplementary archive contains figures only.
evidence_classification: Published evidence; separate from directly reviewed national legal text
